import torch
import torch.nn as nn
import torch.nn.functional as F

class Model(nn.Module):
    def __init__(self, num_classes=1000):
        super(Model, self).__init__()
        self.conv1 = nn.Conv2d(in_channels=3, out_channels=96, kernel_size=11, stride=4, padding=2)
    
    def forward(self, x):
        x = self.conv1(x)
        return x

# Test code
batch_size = 256
num_classes = 1000

def get_inputs():
    return [torch.rand(batch_size, 3, 224, 224)]

def get_init_inputs():
    return [num_classes]

2. The kernel uses 32-bit integer registers `%r1`–`%r50` throughout (for thread IDs, index math, predicates sources, shared-memory addresses), but the `%r` register bank is never declared. Every "Arguments mismatch" and "Illegal operand type" error stems from referencing these undefined `%r` registers.

Line 25 was clearly intended to declare the integer register bank. Replacing `.reg .f32 %f<32>;` with `.reg .b32 %r<64>;` (64 registers to cover the max index `%r50`) fixes the duplicate declaration and provides the missing register bank. No other changes are needed to compile — the float bank `%f<64>` covers `%f1`–`%f41`, `%rd<32>` covers `%rd1`–`%rd10`, and `%p<16>` covers `%p1`–`%p12`. The rest of the kernel (implicit-GEMM structure, cp.async usage, launch glue) is preserved untouched per instructions.
